extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, trade mark and design practitioners, applicants, and litigants (legal professionals and parties involved in patent/trade-mark/design prosecution and litigation)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for prosecution, opposition, petitions to the Privy Council, and civil actions relating to patents, trade marks and designs under the Acts and Privy Council rules (advertising, pleadings, remedies, costs, and evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendor warranty as to genuineness of trade mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any person sells or contracts to sell any chattel or article with any trade mark thereon (or upon associated containers or wrappers etc.), the sale or contract shall be deemed to have been made with a warranty by the vendor that every trade mark upon such chattel or article was genuine and true, and not forged or counterfeit, and not wrongfully used,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This deemed warranty applies unless the contrary is expressed in some writing signed by or on behalf of the vendor and delivered to and accepted by the vendee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendor warranty as to descriptions of quantity/place/etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any chattel or article is sold or contracted to be sold with any description, statement, or other indication respecting number, quantity, measure, or weight, or the place/country of manufacture, the sale/contract is deemed a warranty by the vendor that no such description/statement/indication was in any material respect false or untrue,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The warranty is rebuttable only by a signed writing delivered to and accepted by the vendee that expressly states the contrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court power to order destruction or disposal of counterfeit goods
rubrics_metrics.description: In suits for forging or counterfeiting any trade mark, fraudulently applying any trade mark, or selling/uttering articles with forged/counterfeit or falsely applied trade marks, the court has power to direct every such chattel and article to be destroyed or otherwise disposed of when plaintiff obtains judgment or decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the remedies the court may grant on finding infringement or misuse of trade marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may grant injunctions and punish disobedience as contempt
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions at law the court may, upon giving judgment for the plaintiff, award a writ of injunction commanding the defendant to forbear repeating or committing the wrongful act and disobedience of any such injunction shall be punished as contempt of court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Injunctions may be used to prevent repetition/continuance of wrongful acts of forging, counterfeiting, or false application of trade marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection orders of defendant's manufacture/processes and instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: In suits at law or in equity the court or a judge may make such order as they think fit for the inspection of any manufacture or process carried on by the defendant alleged to use forged/counterfeit marks, and of any chattels, articles, things, and instruments in the defendant's possession or power used or capable of being used for producing or applying such marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person who refuses or neglects to obey an inspection order shall be guilty of contempt of court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of wrongful acts giving rise to action
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrongful acts enumerated include: forging or counterfeiting any trade mark; for sale or manufacture applying any forged or counterfeit trade mark to any chattel/article or to any container/wrapper/label/etc.; selling/uttering/exposing for sale articles with such marks; enclosing/placing/attaching a chattel or article in/on/with any container/thing having thereon any trade mark of another person; applying or attaching to any chattel or article any case/cover/ticket/label/etc. to which a trade mark has been falsely applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person aggrieved by any such wrongful act shall be entitled to maintain an action for damages and for preventing repetition/continuance of the wrongful act and for injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for aggrieved persons (damages and injunctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person aggrieved by the wrongful acts described shall be entitled to maintain an action or suit for damages in respect thereof and for preventing repetition or continuance of the wrongful act and the committal of any similar act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies include damages, injunctions, and orders for destruction/inspection as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs indemnity for defendant in Crown prosecutions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person commences proceedings as plaintiff for or on behalf of Her Majesty for recovering any penalty or sum of money and the defendant obtains judgment, he shall be entitled to recover his costs of suit, which shall include a full indemnity for all the costs, charges, and expenses expended or incurred by him in respect of the action,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court or a judge may direct that only ordinary costs be allowed in place of full indemnity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security for costs where Crown plaintiff lacks grounds or means
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person suing as plaintiff for or on behalf of Her Majesty has no ground for alleging he has been aggrieved and is not resident within jurisdiction or not of sufficient property to pay costs, the court may order that the plaintiff give security (bond/recognizance or deposit of money) for payment of any costs the defendant may recover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a protective measure to prevent vexatious Crown prosecutions without means to satisfy costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy Council petition advertising requirements (sect. 2 / 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party intending to apply by petition under sect. 2 (now sect. 25 Patents Act, 1883) must give public notice by advertising in the London Gazette three times, in three London papers, and three times in some country paper published in the town where or near which he carries on manufacture or resides (or in the county paper), stating the object of the petition and the day he intends to apply for a time to be fixed for hearing (the day must be not less than four weeks from the date of publication of the last advertisement), and that notice of opposition must be given on or before that day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposers must lodge notice at the Council Office on or before the named day and, having lodged notice, are entitled to four weeks' notice of the hearing from the petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy Council petition advertising/caveat requirements (sect. 4 / 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party intending to apply by petition under sect. 4 (now sect. 25 Patents Act, 1883) must, in the advertisements directed by the section, give notice of the day he intends to apply for hearing (not less than four weeks after last Gazette advertisement) and that caveats must be entered on or before such day; any person entering a caveat must enter it at the Council Office on or before that day and then shall be entitled to four weeks' notice of the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors the opposition-notice procedure but governs caveats for extension petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to present petitions after last advertisement
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions under sects. 2 and 4 (now sect. 25) must be presented within one week from the insertion of the last of the required advertisements in the London Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict presentment timing requirement; failure to present within one week may be fatal to the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits of advertisements required with petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: All petitions must be accompanied with affidavits that the advertisements have been inserted according to the provisions of the Act and the Privy Council rules; the matters in such affidavits may be disputed by opposing parties at the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits of compliance are evidence and subject to challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and entitlement to copies for caveators and interested parties
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons entering caveats under sect. 4 and all parties to any former suit or action touching the letters patent in respect of which petitions are presented, and all persons lodging notices of opposition, shall be entitled to be served with copies of petitions presented under the sections, and no application to fix a time for hearing shall be made without affidavit of such service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures interested parties receive documents and service must be sworn before fixing hearing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections grounds to be lodged within a fortnight
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties served with petitions shall lodge at the Council Office, within a fortnight after service, notice of the grounds of their objections to the prayers of the petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely statement of grounds required to preserve objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to papers at own expense
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may have copies of all papers lodged in respect of any application under the Act, at their own expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right to obtain copies for inspection and preparation, subject to paying copying costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxing officer's discretion on payments to expert witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrar of the Privy Council or other officer to whom taxing of costs is referred shall allow or disallow in his discretion all payments made to persons of science or skill examined as witnesses to matters of opinion chiefly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments to expert witnesses are discretionary items in costs taxation and may be disallowed or limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents required for patent extension applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A party applying for an extension of a patent under sect. 4 must lodge six printed copies of the specification and four copies of the balance sheet of expenditure and receipts relating to the patent, which accounts are to be proved on oath at the hearing; where specification not printed and making six copies of drawings would be considerable expense, lodging two copies of the specification and drawing will be deemed sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies must be lodged not less than one week before the day fixed for hearing; the balance sheet must be proved on oath before the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Committee will hear Crown counsel on opposed applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Judicial Committee will hear the Attorney-General or other counsel on behalf of the Crown against granting any application made under either the 2nd or 4th section (now sect. 25) where it is thought fit for the Crown to oppose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crown opposition is considered and Crown counsel will be heard on such matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment of patent or trade mark applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent or to register a trade mark may be abandoned: e.g., by not leaving a complete specification; if not completed within twelve months (unless delay not due to applicant's default); where applicant on opposition fails to send a counter-statement within prescribed time; or if applicant fails to bring opposition before the Court when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural defaults and failure to comply with time limits or requirements lead to abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abridgments of specifications and Comptroller's continuing power
rubrics_metrics.description: Abridgments of specifications are published at the Patent Office and may be continued by the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative handling of published abridgements is within Patent Office/Comptroller discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and advertisement of patent applications/specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of an application for a patent, and acceptance of a complete specification, must be within twelve months and are to be notified/advertised; acceptance of a design or of an application to register a trade mark must be notified to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely acceptance and publication requirements must be met; notifications to applicants follow acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account vs damages election in infringement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions for infringement of a patent (and of a trade mark), the plaintiff may elect between an account of profits and damages; accounts of future profits may be ordered before trial and accounts of past profits at trial; in trade mark actions accounts are restricted to six years' profits; damages cannot be recovered in addition to an account (plaintiff must elect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One joint owner is not entitled to an account as against another; special rules if patent expires before action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on bringing action for patent infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: An action for infringement cannot be brought until the patent is granted, nor for acts done previous to the publication of the complete specification; there are also limitations relating to acts committed during an enlarged time for making a payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaintiff must ensure temporal prerequisites (grant/publication/compliance) are met before suing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial procedure in patent actions (jury, assessor, amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent suits are tried without a jury unless by leave; an assessor may be called in; the specification may be amended during action; particulars of claim/defence and of breaches/objections must be delivered and may be amended by leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may permit amendments and the use of assessors; leave required for jury trial and for adducing evidence of matters not particularized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars required in statements of claim and defence
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of claim must be accompanied by particulars of breaches (object: to state parts of specification infringed and parts of a machine that infringe). Statements of defence must deliver particulars of objections (prior user, names of prior users, general user, prior publication including books/pages/dates/specification numbers, fraud or misrepresentation, that invention is not properly set out, that specification fails to distinguish old from new, that it does not set out the best method, that patent comprises more than one invention not allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No evidence is allowed at trial of infringements for which particulars were not delivered except by leave; generality of particulars cannot be objected to at trial; particulars may be amended (even after trial begun) by leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs in patent actions – certificate requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of patent actions are not allowed unless certified to be proved or to be reasonable; a judge may give such a certificate (including in case of nonsuit or abandonment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary certification governs recovery of costs; judicial discretion applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for piracy of a design (copyright in a design)
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions for infringing copyright in a design the proprietor must elect between recovery of the statutory penalty and an action for damages; a defendant is only liable if knowing that the proprietor did not consent to the application of the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge/non-consent is required for liability; proprietor's election governs remedy pursued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite of registration for trade mark actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For actions for infringing a trade mark, registration is generally a condition precedent to suit (except in the case of old marks), and in some cases a certificate of refusal may be sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimants should ensure statutory registration or established prior (old) mark status before commencing infringement proceedings.
